questions.question: How did the Norman Conquest change the social and political structure of England?
questions.solution_html:
• Implementation of Feudal System – introduced by William the Conqueror - centralizing
  • power and reorganizing land ownership - land was granted to Norman lords (barons) in exchange for
  • military service - English peasantry became serfs, bound to the land and under the control of local
  • lords.
  • Redistribution of Land - nearly all Anglo-Saxon nobles lost their lands, which were
  • redistributed to Norman elites - The Domesday Book (1086) was created to document land
  • ownership and resources, strengthening centralized control.
  • Centralization of Power - the monarchy gained significant authority, with William
  • controlling vast swathes of land directly - castles were built across England to assert Norman
  • dominance and suppress rebellion.
  • Changes in Governance - Anglo-Saxon administrative systems, like the shire and hundred
  • courts, were retained but overseen by Norman officials - Norman-French became the language of the
  • ruling class, law, and administration.
  • Transformation of the Aristocracy - Anglo-Saxon nobility was largely replaced by Norman
  • lords, creating a new elite class loyal to William.
  • Cultural and Legal Shifts - Norman customs and laws, such as primogeniture, were introduced.
  • - ecclesiastical reforms aligned the English Church more closely with Rome, replacing Anglo-Saxon
  • clergy with Normans.
  • Military Reorganization - Norman knights and cavalry replaced the Anglo-Saxon fyrd (militia).
  • - castles fortified Norman control and served as military strongholds.
  • Impact on Language and Culture - Norman-French heavily influenced the English language
  • blending with Anglo-Saxon to form Middle English - architecture, such as Romanesque churches
  • and cathedrals, flourished under Norman influence.
  • Suppression of Rebellion - harsh measures, such as the Harrying of the North (1069–1070)
  • ensured Norman dominance and quashed resistance.
questions.final_answer: ensured Norman dominance and quashed resistance
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) Regular Exam Sem 1, Nov 2024

questions.question: How did the Norman Conquest change the social and political structure of England?
questions.solution_html:
• Implementation of Feudal System – introduced by William the Conqueror - centralizing
  • power and reorganizing land ownership - land was granted to Norman lords (barons) in exchange for
  • military service - English peasantry became serfs, bound to the land and under the control of local
  • lords.
  • Redistribution of Land - nearly all Anglo-Saxon nobles lost their lands, which were
  • redistributed to Norman elites - The Domesday Book (1086) was created to document land
  • ownership and resources, strengthening centralized control.
  • Centralization of Power - the monarchy gained significant authority, with William
  • controlling vast swathes of land directly - castles were built across England to assert Norman
  • dominance and suppress rebellion.
  • Changes in Governance - Anglo-Saxon administrative systems, like the shire and hundred
  • courts, were retained but overseen by Norman officials - Norman-French became the language of the
  • ruling class, law, and administration.
  • Transformation of the Aristocracy - Anglo-Saxon nobility was largely replaced by Norman
  • lords, creating a new elite class loyal to William.
  • Cultural and Legal Shifts - Norman customs and laws, such as primogeniture, were introduced.
  • - ecclesiastical reforms aligned the English Church more closely with Rome, replacing Anglo-Saxon
  • clergy with Normans.
  • Military Reorganization - Norman knights and cavalry replaced the Anglo-Saxon fyrd (militia).
  • - castles fortified Norman control and served as military strongholds.
  • Impact on Language and Culture - Norman-French heavily influenced the English language
  • blending with Anglo-Saxon to form Middle English - architecture, such as Romanesque churches
  • and cathedrals, flourished under Norman influence.
  • Suppression of Rebellion - harsh measures, such as the Harrying of the North (1069–1070)
  • ensured Norman dominance and quashed resistance.
questions.final_answer: ensured Norman dominance and quashed resistance
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) Regular Exam Sem 1, Nov 2024

questions.question: Analyse the role of European explorers in establishing European supremacy.
questions.solution_html:
• . Christopher Columbus - voyages across the Atlantic Ocean - paved the way for European
  • colonization and exploitation of the Americas - Born in Genoa, Italy - embarked on a bold
  • expedition to find a new trade route to Asia by sailing westward - marked the beginning of
  • sustained contact between Europe and the Americas – discovered “the New World”, a term
  • that refers to the Americas -influencing European exploration and colonization -Vasco da
  • Gama, Portuguese explorer - voyages instrumental in establishing a direct maritime route
  • from Europe to India - the first European to reach India by sea, landing in Calicut on the
  • south-western coast of India in 1498. This discovery was ground-breaking as it bypassed the
  • dangerous and long overland routes traditionally used for trade with Asia, particularly for
  • highly sought after spices - route da Gama discovered, around the southern tip of Africa
  • opened up new opportunities for trade and marked the beginning of European imperialism
  • in Asia - led to vast economic gains for Portugal but also solidified its dominance in the
  • spice trade - regarded as a major turning point in the expansion of European colonial
  • empires, establishing an enduring connection between Europe and Asia - Amerigo Vespucci
  • (1454–1512) - Italian explorer, navigator, and cartographer - sailed along the eastern coast
  • of South America, reaching what we now know as Rio de Janeiro and the Río de la Plata.
  • He correctly theorized that these lands were part of a “New World” - altered the way
  • Europeans viewed the world - Ferdinand Magellan circumnavigated the Earth- a discovery
  • that dramatically expanded European geographical knowledge - helping Europeans better
  • understand global trade routes and the world’s geography.
  • {CO1, CO5}
